reason: The assembly audit is the most direct test of address-update overhead: it changes explicit pointer increments to post-indexed loads while keeping the loop trip count and compute group fixed. The end-pointer test also targets loop control, but adds comparisons and end-address setup, so its benefit is less clear. Scratch lifetime is a contained stack-pointer change with low expected benefit. The K-loop schedule and unroll proposals may help, but change more scheduling or register-lifetime details and carry higher correctness risk. The remaining proposals alter traversal, packing, layout, or fallback tails; supplied scores do not establish that these are bottlenecks, and several require broader changes. All recommendations are unmeasured hypotheses; the historical scores are noisy and do not support causal attribution.
